title: What If You Always Drank Your Tea Scalding Hot?

scenes.text: What if you always drank your tea scalding hot? The tea isn't the problem.
In parts of Iran, Turkey and South America, tea and mate are often drunk at about 70 degrees Celsius.
Each scalding sip slightly injures the lining of your food pipe, again and again.
In 2016, the WHO's cancer agency listed drinks above 65 degrees as a probable cause of esophageal cancer.
A study of fifty thousand people in Iran found the risk 90 percent higher at 60 degrees and three cups a day.
That same agency found no clear cancer link for coffee itself. It was never the drink. It's the heat.

description:
In 2016 the International Agency for Research on Cancer classified drinking very hot beverages (above 65 °C) as probably carcinogenic to humans, while finding coffee itself not classifiable as a cause of cancer.
A 2019 study of 50,045 adults in Golestan, Iran, found that drinking 700 ml or more of tea a day at 60 °C or hotter was linked to a 90% higher risk of oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma.
